To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
for a continuous time G lauber dynamics on a hyperbolic graph, if the boundary condition is (+), the mixing time is at most linear in the number of vertices.
the mixing time of the Glauber dynamics on the hyperbolic graphs is linear in n if the boundary is fixed to +, and polynomial in n if the dynamics is free boundary.
the spectral gap is bounded below by some constant independent of n if the boundary condition is (+)-boundary, while it is 1/n if it is free boundary.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the Glauber dynamics on the Ising model with free boundary condition on hyperbolic lattices.
the study of the mixing time of a continuous time Markov process on hyperbolic lattices with free and + boundary conditions, in the regime where the spectral gap is small.
the analysis of the Glauber dynamics for the Ising model at phase coexistence on a class of hyperbolic graphs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the free boundary condition makes the mixing time grow exponentially in n, the (+)-boundary condition makes it grow linearly and the (-)-boundary condition makes the system converge to equilibrium in constant time.
the boundary condition has a dramatic effect on the mixing time, and this is a consequence of the boundary condition being able to influence the dynamics in the bulk.
for a given graph G, the boundary condition has a strong effect on the mixing time of a dynamics if and only if the boundary is large enough to be visible to a random walk on G.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the phase coexistence region, the mixing time of the dynamics on a ball with (+)-boundary is at most logarithmic in n, while the one with free boundary is at least polynomial in n.
the mixing time is linear for the (+)-boundary condition and polynomial for the free boundary condition.

, in the phase coexistence region, for all hyperbolic graphs with v > 4 and s > 3, the mixing time of the Glauber dynamics is linear in n if the boundary is (+)-conditioned, and polynomial in n if the system is free boundary.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the phase coexistence regime of hyperbolic graphs, the mixing time of the Glauber dynamics with free boundary condition is polynomial with exponent depending on the temperature β.
in hyperbolic graphs, the boundary condition has no influence on the mixing time of a continuous time dynamics, in contrast to what happens on regular trees.
the spectral gap is independent of the boundary condition if the latter does not influence the dynamics on a large fraction of the graph.
